# ROADMAP #29(d) — cross-appropriation lineage: a negative result

**Outcome: ship nothing.** Eleven candidates were generated by a rule designed
against the existing `ba_maturation_same_title` inference, then adversarially
verified by three independent lenses each (33 agents, 0 errors). **Every one was
refuted by a majority.** No edge shipped.

This document exists so the rule is not rebuilt. The candidates looked good —
GBSD/Sentinel, Precision Strike Missile, Combat Rescue Helicopter, AMPV, NGJ,
JDAM, Aegis BMD, CIRCM. All are real programs. All really do have both an RDT&E
PE and a Procurement line. The inference drawn from that is still wrong.

---

## The rule that was tested

Modelled on `infer.py::ba_maturation_same_title`, a candidate required all of:

1. RDT&E side matches `^06\d{5}\w*$` — a real PE, not a bare numeric
2. Procurement side is a P-1 line and not a synthetic `-L<n>` rollup artifact
3. Procurement `pe_bli` unique by title
4. Same organization on both sides
5. A funding hand-off: RDT&E falls in the FY the procurement line rises

Filtering, measured against the warehouse:

```
20  title-matched (RDT&E PE, P-1 line) pairs
 -3  procurement key not unique      4217, 4248, 3011
 -4  no funding hand-off
 -2  cross-service title collision   0604287F: AF RDT&E -> Navy procurement
 = 11 candidates
```

Filters 3 and 4 were themselves lessons from earlier work — #29(a) established
that bare numerics name more than one program, and the same-agency guard already
existed in the RDT&E rule because same-title-across-services is coincidence.

---

## Why all eleven fell

### 1. Concurrent development and production is normal, and it is not a hand-off

This is the finding that kills the whole approach. A DoD program carries an RDT&E
line **and** a Procurement line **simultaneously, for its entire life**. They are
two permanent parallel appropriation identities of one program, not a predecessor
and a successor.

- **Aegis BMD** — co-funded in all ten editions PB2017–PB2026. Verified directly:
  FY2024 `0603892C` $2,512.9M / `MD09` $1,531.3M; FY2025 $1,929.3M / $862.0M;
  FY2026 **$3,888.4M / $796.5M**. In the claimed FY2025 hand-off the RDT&E line
  *rises 53%* while procurement *collapses 77%* — the inverse of a maturation.
  `MD09`'s own P-40 gives the real reason: *"the termination of Standard Missile-3
  (SM-3) Block IB new production"*.
- **Combat Rescue Helicopter** — procurement funded since FY2019, its own P-40
  dating Milestone C to Sep 2019, co-funded through FY2026. At the claimed
  hand-off procurement is *falling* ($1.21B → $107.5M) while RDT&E *rises*.
- **Air Traffic Control** — procurement was already enacted at $22.3M in FY2016,
  before the claimed hand-off; at FY2018 the RDT&E line rose while procurement
  went to zero.

### 2. Procurement key renumbering fabricates a rise from zero

Edition-local P-1 keys change between books. A line that existed for years under
one key appears "new" under another, and a taper detector reads that as money
arriving.

- **AMPV** — `2033A-ARMY-L1/L2` became `2944G80819` in PB2024. The "FY2024
  hand-off" is the rename. The two lines were co-funded FY2018–FY2022, and the
  RDT&E line was already at zero in FY2023, so nothing tapered into it.
- **CIRCM** — `2031A-ARMY-L##` became `5399AZ3537` in PB2024. The procurement
  line runs continuously in account 2031A/BA 04 back to PB2018 at
  $168.8M–$288.2M/yr, and in FY2024 it *falls* while RDT&E stays flat.

**The detector was reading identifier changes as money movements.** That failure
mode is not specific to cross-appropriation and is worth remembering anywhere a
rule compares series across editions.

### 3. The corpus already contains stated evidence that contradicts the inference

- **Combat Training Ranges** — the claimed FY2019 hand-off does not exist:
  verified directly, `834190`'s FY2019 base, OCO and total are **all $0.0**; it
  fell to zero rather than rising. Worse, `834190`'s own P-1 narrative names
  **PE 0207429F** as the source of its funding — a different program element
  entirely, stated in the document, contradicting the edge outright.

That last case is the sharpest argument against shipping any of this. The site
already had the answer, in a cited narrative, and the inference disagreed with it.

---

## What was learned that is worth keeping

- **A shared title plus a same-organization guard plus a funding taper is not
  sufficient evidence of a money transfer.** All three held on eleven candidates
  and all eleven were wrong.
- **Co-funding is disqualifying.** If both lines carry money in the same year,
  they are parallel identities, not successive ones. Any future attempt at this
  should test co-funding *first* — it eliminated most candidates instantly and
  cheaply.
- **Cross-edition key stability must be established before comparing series.**
  A "rise from zero" is meaningless if the key did not exist under that name
  before.
- The existing **Inferred** tier stays as it is: deterministic RDT&E-only
  BA-maturation, same agency, adjacent BA, shared title, funding taper — 3 edges,
  dashed amber, never summed. It survives because BA maturation happens *within*
  one appropriation, where sequential funding is the norm rather than the
  exception.

## Method note

The eleven candidates were measured by the orchestrator before any agent ran, so
the verification judged a fixed population rather than an open question. Each
candidate was then judged on three lenses — identity (same program or shared
title?), money (does spend actually hand off?), and refutation (default to
refuted unless positively established) — with a majority refutation dropping it.
The workflow's `ship-nothing` branch was written into the script before it ran,
so "no" was a first-class outcome rather than a failure state.

33 agents, 0 errors, ~$0 marginal (no paid extraction; deterministic queries).
